resources.title: ASSIST Quick Search
resources.use: Official starting point for defense and federal specifications, standards, and related documents.
resources.check: Search the project’s document numbers. Check revision history, status, amendments, and the edition required by the contract.

resources.title: MIL-STD-810 — Environmental engineering and laboratory tests
resources.use: A source to investigate when environmental conditions and testing are part of a defense project.
resources.check: Select relevant methods with the responsible engineer; this is not a universal test checklist for every military product.

resources.title: MIL-STD-2073-1 — Military packaging
resources.use: A source to investigate when the project has military packaging requirements.
resources.check: Read the contract’s packaging requirements and confirm the required edition before preparing the package.

resources.title: MIL-STD-129 — Shipment and storage marking
resources.use: A source to investigate for military shipment and storage markings.
resources.check: Check the contract and any additional customer marking requirements.

resources.title: ISO 9001 — Quality management
resources.use: Publisher’s page for the general quality-management standard.
resources.check: Check the current edition and which edition the customer requires. Obtain authorized access before using the full text; check permission for AI use.

resources.title: IAQG — Aerospace quality standards
resources.use: Publisher’s directory for the 9100 family and related aerospace quality standards.
resources.check: Choose the standard for the work and customer requirement; follow the publisher’s access and licensing instructions.

resources.title: IATF 16949 — Automotive quality
resources.use: Official starting point for the automotive quality-management standard.
resources.check: Check current publications, interpretations, and customer-specific requirements before applying it.

resources.title: ISO 13485 — Medical-device quality
resources.use: Publisher’s page for medical-device quality management.
resources.check: Check product and market applicability separately. Obtain authorized access and check permission for AI use.

resources.title: USPTO — Patent basics
resources.use: Official patent background and links to the application process.
resources.check: Use current official information for the relevant patent question; keep unresolved issues for the legal role’s professional-review packet.

resources.title: USPTO — Find a patent practitioner
resources.use: Official route to the register of active patent attorneys and agents.
resources.check: Confirm the assigned practitioner’s active USPTO registration. For an attorney, also check state-bar standing. Ask about technical experience, conflicts, who does the work, and a written scope and fee estimate.
resources.verification_note: Official practitioner lookup confirmed during the September 30 legal-resource research.

resources.title: Angel Capital Association — Member directory
resources.use: Find angel groups and investment platforms, then visit each group's own site to check geography, industry and application process.
resources.check: ACA is a directory, not a source of direct funding. Check entrepreneur fees, eligibility and information-sharing terms before applying.
resources.verification_note: Official directory explicitly says ACA is not a direct funding source and advises entrepreneurs to investigate presentation or platform fees.

resources.title: SBIR / STTR — Federal research funding
resources.use: Starting point for participating agencies and research-funding opportunities.
resources.check: Check current program availability, the specific agency solicitation, eligibility, and deadline; do not assume an opportunity is open.

resources.title: SBA — Business planning and market research
resources.use: Start with the market-research section: define customers, compare competing solutions and test demand, pricing and market size.
resources.check: Combine published data with interviews or other direct research. Record assumptions and sources before using market estimates in a funding plan.
resources.verification_note: Former business-guide market-research URL redirects to this current hub; it contains the full market research and competitive analysis section.

resources.title: NIST MEP — Manufacturing assistance centers
resources.use: Find manufacturing assistance centers by location.
resources.check: Ask the relevant center about current services and local supplier resources; a listing is not a quote or supplier qualification.

resources.title: NIST NVLAP — Accredited laboratory directory
resources.use: Find testing and calibration laboratories and their accreditation scopes.
resources.check: Verify the exact test method and current scope. Laboratory accreditation is not a claim that your product is certified.

resources.title: MIL-STD-461 — Electromagnetic interference
resources.use: Military requirements for equipment and subsystem electromagnetic emissions and susceptibility.
resources.check: Select applicable tests from the contract and equipment/platform requirements; verify the required revision in ASSIST. This is separate from enclosure IP protection.

resources.title: UL Standards & Engagement — Electrical standards
resources.use: Find UL standards for the product: UL 508A for industrial control panels; UL 50 and UL 50E for electrical enclosures; UL 62368-1 for audio/video and information/communication technology equipment.
resources.check: Confirm product scope, market, edition, and certification route. A compliant component or enclosure does not certify the whole product.

resources.title: IEC — Electrical product standards
resources.use: International standards: IEC 60204-1 for machinery electrical equipment; IEC 61010-1 for measurement, control and laboratory equipment; IEC 62368-1 for AV/ICT equipment; IEC 60335-1 for household appliances; IEC 60601-1 for medical electrical equipment.
resources.check: Choose the relevant family, particular parts, amendments and national adoption. These are starting points, not a checklist that applies to every product.

resources.title: CENELEC — European electrical standards (EN)
resources.use: Starting point for European electrotechnical standards. EN identifies a European standard; EN IEC indicates a European adoption of an IEC standard.
resources.check: Confirm the actual European/national edition and any deviations for the target market. IEC and EN are not military standards. A military contract may reference them.

resources.title: IEC 60529 — Enclosure protection (IP Code)
resources.use: Publisher’s source for protection against access to hazardous parts, solid objects, dust and harmful water ingress.
resources.check: Use the full applicable standard and actual product test evidence for a rating claim. Read the IP quick guide for orientation; distinguish dust protection, jets and immersion.

resources.title: NFPA 70 — National Electrical Code (NEC)
resources.use: Reference for electrical installations in the United States.
resources.check: Check the edition adopted at the installation location and applicable local requirements. Installation rules are distinct from product certification.

resources.title: NFPA 79 — Electrical Standard for Industrial Machinery
resources.use: Starting point for electrical equipment of industrial machines.
resources.check: Confirm machine scope and the required edition; coordinate with the applicable installation and product standards.

resources.title: NEMA enclosure Types — ANSI catalog
resources.use: Catalog entry for ANSI/NEMA 250 enclosure Type requirements, commonly encountered alongside UL 50E.
resources.check: This linked 2020 edition is labeled historical by ANSI. Check current replacement/status and the project-required edition before use. Do not convert an IP code directly into a NEMA Type or a certification claim.
resources.source: ANSI catalog; NEMA is the content provider

resources.title: McMaster-Carr — Hardware and ready-made CAD
resources.use: A broad hardware catalog and a convenient first design reference when it has the needed part and CAD model. Existing CAD can save the designer from drawing the part. You may buy from any supplier you choose.
resources.check: Send the designer the part link and number when selecting here. Verify dimensions, material/grade, finish, tolerances and model availability. Keep the catalog reference separate from the chosen purchasing source; respect current CAD-use terms.

resources.title: Fastenal — Procurement and production supply
resources.use: A source for Soren to compare for ongoing fastener/hardware supply, sourcing and inventory needs as quantities grow.
resources.check: Compare an exact specification and approved part cross-reference, delivered cost, quantities, lead time and required documentation. Obtain the engineering role’s review of substitutions; a similar appearance is not proof of equivalence.

resources.title: Xometry
resources.use: CNC machining, 3D printing, sheet metal and molding through an on-demand manufacturing platform.
resources.check: Compare the same drawing/model revision, material, finish, quantity, tolerances, inspection needs, delivered price and lead time. Verify current capability for this part; a catalog listing is not a qualified supplier or a quote.

resources.title: Protolabs
resources.use: Prototype and production services including injection molding, CNC machining, 3D printing and sheet metal.
resources.check: Compare the same drawing/model revision, material, finish, quantity, tolerances, inspection needs, delivered price and lead time. Verify current capability for this part; a catalog listing is not a qualified supplier or a quote.

resources.title: JLCPCB — Circuit boards and assembly
resources.use: PCB fabrication and assembly for electronic prototypes; choose board specifications and assembly inputs for the actual design.
resources.check: Compare the same drawing/model revision, material, finish, quantity, tolerances, inspection needs, delivered price and lead time. Verify current capability for this part; a catalog listing is not a qualified supplier or a quote.

resources.title: JLC3DP — 3D printing
resources.use: JLC’s 3D-printing service for prototype parts. Check available processes, materials and finishes.
resources.check: Compare the same drawing/model revision, material, finish, quantity, tolerances, inspection needs, delivered price and lead time. Verify current capability for this part; a catalog listing is not a qualified supplier or a quote.

resources.title: JLCCNC — Machined parts
resources.use: JLC’s CNC-machining service for custom parts. Check dimensions, materials and tolerances.
resources.check: Compare the same drawing/model revision, material, finish, quantity, tolerances, inspection needs, delivered price and lead time. Verify current capability for this part; a catalog listing is not a qualified supplier or a quote.

resources.title: Fictiv
resources.use: Additional source for custom parts, including machining, molding and 3D printing.
resources.check: Compare the same drawing/model revision, material, finish, quantity, tolerances, inspection needs, delivered price and lead time. Verify current capability for this part; a catalog listing is not a qualified supplier or a quote.

resources.title: Quickparts
resources.use: Additional source for prototype and production parts, including 3D printing, machining and molding.
resources.check: Compare the same drawing/model revision, material, finish, quantity, tolerances, inspection needs, delivered price and lead time. Verify current capability for this part; a catalog listing is not a qualified supplier or a quote.

resources.title: SBA — Launch your business
resources.use: An official roadmap for structure, location, business names, registration, tax IDs, licenses, bank accounts and insurance.
resources.check: Use it to identify the steps for your situation, then confirm requirements with the responsible state, local or federal agency. A formation service is optional; it is not the government.
resources.verification_note: Official launch hub describes the business formation topics and links to state resources.

resources.title: SBA — Find your state registration office
resources.use: Find the state or territory office responsible for business registration without starting from a search advertisement.
resources.check: Select the correct jurisdiction, follow the agency link, and verify the filing type, actual government fee and renewals. A registered-agent service and the state filing office are different things.
resources.verification_note: Official state registration lookup links to the state offices.

resources.title: USA.gov — State and territory governments
resources.use: A trusted route to state government websites for taxes, licenses and local agency information.
resources.check: Continue to the agency for the actual task. Some official portals use a different domain; verify that the government page sends you there before submitting information.
resources.verification_note: USAGov lists all state and territory government starting points.

resources.title: IRS — Get an EIN directly, for free
resources.use: The official IRS starting point for an employer identification number (EIN). The IRS does not charge for an EIN.
resources.check: Check eligibility and the responsible party’s authority. For an LLC or corporation, follow the IRS’s instructions about state formation first. Save the confirmation with company records.
resources.verification_note: IRS explicitly states the EIN is free, warns about paid websites, and explains eligibility and entity formation order.

resources.title: IRS — Starting a business and federal taxes
resources.use: Federal tax starting points for new businesses, including structure, taxes, records and tax-year choices.
resources.check: Match the current guidance to the actual entity, activities and tax year; review state and local requirements separately with the appropriate adviser.
resources.verification_note: IRS starting-a-business page lists federal tax basics and directs state-level questions to state websites.

resources.title: IRS Publication 583 — Starting a business and keeping records
resources.use: A starting reference for business records and bookkeeping responsibilities.
resources.check: Check the publication date and current tax-year guidance. Keep business transactions and supporting records organized; confirm retention rules for the type of record.
resources.verification_note: IRS publication covers starting a business, recordkeeping and tax records.

resources.title: FinCEN — Check current beneficial ownership rules
resources.use: The agency’s current source for beneficial ownership information (BOI) reporting and exemptions.
resources.check: Check current applicability before filing or paying anyone. At this review, FinCEN says U.S. companies are exempt; foreign-formed entities registered in the U.S. need a separate applicability check. Avoid old blanket claims that every LLC must file.
resources.verification_note: FinCEN page includes August 11, 2026 final-rule alert and U.S.-company exemption. Rules must be rechecked when used.

resources.title: FTC — Scams targeting small businesses
resources.use: Recognize fake invoices, government impersonation, misleading services and other scams aimed at businesses.
resources.check: Verify unexpected demands through a known official contact or website. Do not use the payment link or telephone number in a suspicious message to verify that same message.
resources.verification_note: FTC guide covers business and government impersonation and fraudulent grant offers.

resources.title: NIST — Small Business Cybersecurity Corner
resources.use: Practical cybersecurity starting points for a small company’s accounts, devices, data and suppliers.
resources.check: Choose resources for the actual business and current risks. A guide is not a security certification; keep account permissions, backups and recovery responsibilities explicit.
resources.verification_note: NIST maintains a collection of small-business cybersecurity guidance.

resources.title: SAM.gov — Entity registration and Unique Entity ID
resources.use: Official registration for organizations pursuing federal awards, or a Unique Entity ID when that alone is appropriate. SAM registration and renewal are free.
resources.check: Start by typing sam.gov. Choose the correct registration purpose, follow Login.gov from SAM, and confirm the current record and renewal instructions. Paid third-party help is optional; it is not a government registration fee.
resources.verification_note: GSA states SAM registration and renewal are free. SAM entity-registration page describes the current routes and links to Login.gov.

resources.title: APEX Accelerators — Government contracting assistance
resources.use: Find local assistance for government contracting and SAM registration. SAM.gov links to this program for free registration help.
resources.check: Follow the APEX link from SAM.gov to confirm the destination. Check your local center’s service area and what assistance is included; this is an example of a legitimate program on a .us domain.
resources.verification_note: SAM.gov entity-registration page explicitly links APEX Accelerators as an official assistance resource and states free help completing SAM registration.

resources.title: DLA — Getting started as a supplier
resources.use: The Defense Logistics Agency’s route into supplier registration, SAM/CAGE information and its bidding systems.
resources.check: Start on the DLA .mil page and follow its current links. Match registrations, capabilities and documentation to the actual opportunity; registration does not guarantee a contract.
resources.verification_note: Official DLA search-indexed page describes SAM, CAGE, APEX and DIBBS. Direct automated fetch unavailable; indexed agency content reviewed.

resources.title: Grants.gov — Search federal funding opportunities
resources.use: Search the official federal grant opportunity directory by eligibility and subject.
resources.check: Confirm applicant type, purpose, dates and registrations in the actual notice. Not every grant accepts a for-profit startup. Ignore unsolicited messages claiming you have already won a grant.
resources.verification_note: Official Grants.gov search and grant-fraud guidance; no claim any particular opportunity is open.

resources.title: CPSC — Small business product-safety resources
resources.use: Starting guidance for consumer-product safety requirements and the Small Business Ombudsman.
resources.check: Identify product type and intended users before selecting rules, tests, certificates or labeling. Follow the applicable rule and actual evidence; do not assume one guide covers every product.
resources.verification_note: CPSC small-business page points to product-area guidance and the Small Business Ombudsman.

resources.title: USPTO — Patent Pro Bono Program
resources.use: Find regional programs that match eligible inventors and small businesses with volunteer patent professionals.
resources.check: Check your regional program’s income, invention, and training requirements, availability, and any costs you must pay.
resources.verification_note: Opened official program page; it describes regional eligibility and links to the coverage map. Placement and acceptance are not guaranteed.

resources.title: USPTO — Law school patent and trademark clinics
resources.use: Find supervised law-school clinics offering free patent or trademark legal services to accepted clients.
resources.check: Confirm geographic eligibility, patent versus trademark coverage, intake availability, deadlines, and responsibility for filing costs.
resources.verification_note: Opened current official directory of participating clinics with subject and geographic coverage; each clinic controls acceptance.

resources.title: USPTO — Patent Public Search
resources.use: Search published U.S. patent applications and patents, with beginner and advanced tools and tutorials.
resources.check: Save document numbers and relevant passages for the legal role. A search alone does not establish patentability or freedom to sell; check current access requirements.
resources.verification_note: Opened official landing page linking Basic and Advanced search. It announces account sign-in beginning November 7, 2026; avoid promising permanent anonymous access.

resources.title: USPTO — Patent and Trademark Resource Centers
resources.use: Find a library specialist who can help you learn patent and trademark search tools and locate official information.
resources.check: Ask about local appointments and classes. Resource-center staff provide research guidance, not legal advice.
resources.verification_note: Opened official network overview and local-center locator link; page explicitly distinguishes search assistance from legal advice.

resources.title: USPTO — Trademark basics
resources.use: Start researching protection for a business name, product name, or logo and follow official registration guidance.
resources.check: Review name availability with the legal role before investing in branding; follow the official search and filing links and verify notices directly with USPTO.
resources.verification_note: Opened official trademark basics page with linked federal registration guidance.

resources.title: American Bar Association — Find Legal Help
resources.use: Find state lawyer-referral and licensing resources for company formation, contracts, and other legal questions.
resources.check: Use the relevant state licensing authority to check a lawyer’s current standing. Confirm business-law experience, conflicts, scope, and fees directly.
resources.verification_note: Opened association directory with lawyer referral and licensing routes; ABA does not itself provide individual legal representation or a performance endorsement.

resources.title: Schwegman Lundberg & Woessner — Mechanical patents
resources.use: A patent-firm candidate for mechanical and electromechanical inventions, IP strategy, and patent preparation and prosecution.
resources.check: Candidate to interview. Check the assigned practitioner’s USPTO registration, attorney state-bar standing, technical experience, conflicts, and written scope and fees before engagement.
resources.verification_note: Opened mechanical practice page and firm overview; prior mechanical-electromechanical URL redirects here. Firm-authored evidence supports practice fit, not independent quality or current availability.

resources.title: Wolf Greenfield — Mechanical technologies
resources.use: A patent-firm candidate for consumer products, industrial equipment, robotics, design protection, and product-clearance questions.
resources.check: Candidate to interview. Check the assigned practitioner’s USPTO registration, attorney state-bar standing, technical experience, conflicts, and written scope and fees before engagement.
resources.verification_note: Opened practice page listing mechanical/electromechanical industries and startup robotics experience. Firm-authored evidence supports scope; outcomes, affordability, and individual practitioners have not been independently vetted.

resources.title: Rocky Mountain Patent / Hall Estill — Inventors and startups
resources.use: A patent-firm candidate focused on inventors and startups, with stated mechanical and electrical expertise and patent-prosecution services.
resources.check: Candidate to interview. Check the assigned practitioner’s USPTO registration, attorney state-bar standing, technical experience, conflicts, and written scope and fees before engagement.
resources.verification_note: Opened firm home page; it identifies Rocky Mountain Patent as an integrated patent-prosecution group within Hall Estill and lists inventor/startup, mechanical, and electrical work. Confirm current engagement entity and assigned counsel.

resources.title: SendCutSend — Cut and bent sheet parts
resources.use: Candidate for laser-cut or routed sheet parts, brackets, bending and finishing.
resources.check: Match material, thickness, bend radius, hole placement and finish to the shop’s design rules. Quote the same approved revision and ask what inspection is included.
resources.verification_note: Official service catalog lists sheet cutting, CNC machining, bending, hardware insertion and finishes.

resources.title: Protocase — Custom enclosures and machined parts
resources.use: Candidate for prototype electronic enclosures, front panels, sheet-metal assemblies and CNC-machined housings.
resources.check: Confirm dimensions, mounting and connector cutouts, ventilation, finish and markings. Specify any required inspection; enclosure fabrication alone does not establish an IP rating or product certification.
resources.verification_note: Official products and services page lists sheet-metal enclosures, panels, CNC machining and 3D printing.

resources.title: MacroFab — Circuit-board assembly
resources.use: Candidate for sourcing components and assembling electronic circuit boards from prototype through production.
resources.check: Supply matching board files, parts list (BOM), placement data and revision. Agree substitutions, test coverage, assembly criteria, programming, factory location and export-data handling before uploading restricted files.
resources.verification_note: Official platform describes PCB assembly quoting, component sourcing, manufacturing/test tracking and revision comparison.

resources.title: DigiKey — Electronic components and design tools
resources.use: Electronic-component sourcing plus schematic, footprint and 3D-model tools for circuit development.
resources.check: Verify the exact manufacturer part number, datasheet, package/footprint, lifecycle and stock. Check CAD models against the datasheet; approve substitutes and compare quantity breaks and delivered cost.
resources.verification_note: Official design-tools page connects tools to component inventory and lists schematic, simulation and CAD-library resources.

resources.title: MISUMI — Configurable automation components
resources.use: Candidate for configurable mechanical parts, linear-motion and factory-automation components with downloadable CAD.
resources.check: Record the complete configured part number. Check dimensions, material, load, fits, tolerances and delivery; match the CAD configuration to the part being purchased.
resources.verification_note: Official catalog lists configurable components, automation, electrical/control categories and 3D CAD downloads.

resources.title: AutomationDirect — Controls, pneumatics and vision
resources.use: Candidate catalog for PLCs, motor control, sensors, vision devices and lighting, pneumatic tubing, valves, grippers and vacuum parts.
resources.check: Check voltage, I/O and communication compatibility, air pressure/flow, fittings and environment. For vision, confirm field of view, lighting and actual sample performance. Have the responsible engineer review safety functions separately.
resources.verification_note: Official catalog lists programmable controllers, motion, vision, pneumatic parts and sensors; dedicated pneumatic overview and vision catalog also verified.

resources.title: Festo — Vacuum handling and suction cups
resources.use: Candidate for vacuum generators, suction cups, vacuum grippers and accessories when designing handling equipment.
resources.check: Select for workpiece material, surface, shape, mass and motion. Confirm vacuum level, leakage/flow, cup wear and loss-of-vacuum behavior with the application engineer; test on real parts.
resources.verification_note: Official US catalog covers generators, suction cups/grippers and supporting vacuum accessories.

resources.title: Thomas — Find manufacturing suppliers
resources.use: Search for machine shops, fabricators and other industrial suppliers by capability and location; useful for building a local shortlist.
resources.check: A directory entry or badge is not project qualification. Verify current equipment, materials, tolerance capability, inspection, certification scope, references and willingness to take a small order.
resources.verification_note: Directory operator describes capability profiles and location/certification filters. Badge documentation distinguishes basic business validation from project-specific qualification.

resources.title: FabLabs — Find a local fabrication lab
resources.use: Find nearby fabrication labs for early mockups, access to tools, training and hands-on help.
resources.check: Confirm the lab is active and ask about public access, equipment, training, fees, commercial work and confidentiality. A shared makerspace is not automatically a production or inspection supplier.
resources.verification_note: Official network directory provides lab profiles and list/map search by location.

resources.title: Census Business Builder
resources.use: Explore U.S. customer demographics and business activity by location and industry; download maps and reports for market research.
resources.check: Record the data year, geography and industry definition. Published statistics support research; confirm demand by speaking with prospective customers.
resources.verification_note: Official tool page describes demographic/economic data, geographic comparisons, interactive maps and downloadable reports.

resources.title: Google Trends
resources.use: Compare search interest in product terms across time and places to explore terminology, seasonality and possible customer questions.
resources.check: Scores show relative search interest, not sales, market size or an absolute count of customers. Record region, dates and search terms.
resources.verification_note: Google's data FAQ explains sampled search data and normalized 0–100 interest; it warns that Trends is not polling data.

resources.title: Google — Search Engine Optimization Starter Guide
resources.use: Learn how to make a website easier for people and search engines to understand and discover.
resources.check: Use the guide to improve useful content and site structure. Following it does not guarantee indexing or a particular search position.
resources.verification_note: Official Search Central guide covers SEO fundamentals and states that indexing and first-place ranking are not guaranteed.

resources.title: HubSpot Academy — Digital marketing course
resources.use: An introductory course covering marketing strategy, content, search, email, social media and advertising.
resources.check: The listed course is free and uses a HubSpot Academy account. Distinguish educational material from optional paid HubSpot products.
resources.verification_note: Official page labels this a free certification course and identifies small business owners as an audience.

resources.title: FTC — Advertising and marketing guidance
resources.use: Check product claims, endorsements, reviews, influencers, Made in USA statements and other advertising topics before publishing.
resources.check: Choose the guidance matching the product and channel. Keep evidence for claims and review relevant disclosure rules with the responsible specialist.
resources.verification_note: Official FTC topic hub links advertising basics, endorsements, environmental/health claims, origin claims and online marketing guidance.

resources.title: FTC — Commercial email (CAN-SPAM) guide
resources.use: Use the official checklist when planning promotional email, including business-to-business campaigns.
resources.check: Review sender information, subject lines, postal-address and unsubscribe requirements. Also check applicable state, international and platform rules.
resources.verification_note: Official guide covers commercial messages, explicitly including business-to-business email, and lists compliance requirements.

resources.title: SCORE — Find a business mentor
resources.use: Find volunteer mentors by expertise, industry and location to discuss business plans, marketing, operations or finance.
resources.check: Mentoring is free; some workshops or premium programs cost money. Look for experience relevant to your business and check each program's price.
resources.verification_note: SCORE FAQ confirms volunteer mentors, free mentoring, and both free and paid education. SBA's Resource Partners page identifies SCORE as a nonprofit.

resources.title: SBA — Local business help and SBDCs
resources.use: Find a nearby Small Business Development Center or other SBA partner for planning, operations, market research and finance guidance.
resources.check: Start at SBA.gov and follow its directory to the local center. Confirm service area, appointment process and any training fees.
resources.verification_note: Current SBA pages describe free or low-cost local counseling/training and SBDC advising for existing and pre-venture businesses; linked partner sites may use .org or .edu.

resources.title: Golden Seeds — Women-led company funding
resources.use: An angel network to investigate for U.S.-domiciled, early-stage companies in technology, healthcare and consumer sectors with a woman in an operating C-suite role.
resources.check: Review leadership/equity, traction and sector criteria. A non-refundable $50 application fee is listed; confirm the current fee and eligibility before submitting.
resources.verification_note: Official criteria require U.S. domicile and a woman in an influential operating C-suite role with appropriate equity. Application page lists a $50 non-refundable fee.

resources.title: TCA Venture Group — Funding applications
resources.use: Explore seed and early growth funding across technology-related sectors in the U.S. and Canada, with a strong Southern California focus.
resources.check: Choose the relevant chapter and check its location, industry and traction criteria. Fee terms differ: Orange County lists an administrative application fee despite general no-fee wording.
resources.verification_note: Official page identifies U.S./Canada scope, California preference, market traction and chapter-specific eligibility. It contains conflicting general no-fee wording and a specific Orange County admin-fee statement.

resources.title: Band of Angels — Seed investment
resources.use: A California-based angel network considering U.S.-registered seed technology and life-science companies, including hardware and other technical products.
resources.check: Review technology, market and stage fit. Its FAQ allows U.S. companies beyond Silicon Valley and lists no submission or presentation fees; check current terms before applying.
resources.verification_note: Official investment page states seed high-tech/life-science focus and no presenting fees; About FAQ says U.S. registration required, nationwide investment continues and no submission fees.

resources.title: Kickstarter — Creator Handbook
resources.use: Plan a rewards-based crowdfunding campaign: tell the story, build rewards, promote it, communicate with backers and prepare fulfillment.
resources.check: Review current project eligibility, platform fees and delivery responsibilities before choosing crowdfunding. Budget manufacturing, shipping and campaign costs.
resources.verification_note: Official handbook provides sections on getting started, funding, fulfillment, story, promotion, rewards and backer communications.

resources.title: NIST MEP — Product design and development
resources.use: Find help with market validation, prototypes, materials, durability and commercialization.
resources.check: AN Creation’s project checkpoints are an original synthesis; NIST does not prescribe these forms.

resources.title: NIOSH — Ergonomic risk factors and checklists
resources.use: Screen posture, force, repetition, handling and task conditions when preparing a user trial.
resources.check: Workplace guidance must be adapted to the task and intended users; it is not universal consumer-product clearance.

resources.title: NIOSH — Non-powered hand-tool selection guide
resources.use: Practical hand-tool ergonomics background for grip and task evaluation.
resources.check: Scope is non-powered hand tools; do not transfer its dimensions to every product.

resources.title: Protolabs — Process-specific design tips
resources.use: Start process-specific DFM research for machining, molding and other manufacturing methods.
resources.check: Supplier guidance depends on geometry, material and process. Confirm the selected manufacturer’s capabilities; automated DFM is not full design approval.

resources.title: Protolabs — Uniform wall thickness in molded parts
resources.use: Investigate molded-part walls, sink, warpage and geometry tradeoffs.
resources.check: Numerical examples are supplier/process guidance, not a universal specification.

resources.title: NASA — Requirements verification matrix
resources.use: A useful model for linking each requirement to a source and verification method.
resources.check: Adapt the evidence discipline to project scale; NASA procedures are not mandatory consumer-product certification.

resources.title: NASA — Product realization, verification and validation
resources.use: Understand checking specified requirements versus intended use.
resources.check: Record actual configuration, method, evidence and limits; a single prototype does not establish production consistency.

resources.title: NIST MEP — Supplier scouting inquiry fields
resources.use: Examples of technical and commercial information needed to identify manufacturing capability.
resources.check: The public form displayed an expired OMB date during this review. Use fields as preparation; confirm the current submission route with a local MEP center before submitting.

resources.title: USPTO — Patent rights, ownership and infringement
resources.use: Understand exclusion rights, ownership and the separate infringement question.
resources.check: Having a patent is not affirmative permission to make or sell a product. Seek a product/territory-specific analysis when freedom to operate matters.

resources.title: USPTO — Design patents
resources.use: Compare ornamental-design protection with utility protection for function.
resources.check: Identify the actual subject matter and jurisdiction; do not infer patentability from a checklist.

resources.title: USPTO — Provisional patent applications

resources.use: Wisconsin manufacturing improvement and consulting; a local complement to the existing national NIST MEP directory.
resources.check: Confirm geography, capabilities, scope, fees and confidentiality before inquiries or sharing designs. Funding announcements do not establish free client services.

resources.title: AN Creation — Design principles: people, form and use
resources.use: Practical review of usefulness, clarity, interaction, inclusive use, ergonomics, durability and lifecycle; includes a 16-area editable worksheet.
resources.check: Use relevant prompts quietly, link judgments to evidence, requirements and risks, and plan representative user trials. Scores, population percentiles and medical-device sample counts are not universal proof of success.

resources.title: Vitsœ — Dieter Rams: good design
resources.use: Consider usefulness, clarity, restraint, honest presentation, enduring quality and environmental consequences.
resources.check: Design philosophy prompts, not numerical acceptance criteria or proof of product performance.

resources.title: Don Norman — Interaction, signifiers and feedback
resources.use: Distinguish possible actions from cues that communicate them; review feedback and the user's mental model.
resources.check: The article discusses touch and gesture systems; adapt the interaction ideas to the actual physical product and test them.

resources.title: IDSA — What is industrial design?
resources.use: Understand the connection between appearance, function, manufacturability and the user's overall experience.
resources.check: A profession/process overview, not a prescribed six-stage standard or validated engineering package.

resources.title: NC State — Principles of Universal Design
resources.use: Review access, flexibility, clarity, perceivable information, error tolerance, effort and space for use.
resources.check: Design guidance from the originating institution; it is not accessibility certification or proof that every user is accommodated.

resources.title: NIOSH — Ergonomics overview
resources.use: Consider posture, force, repetition and the interaction between a person and the task.
resources.check: Occupational guidance; adapt it to the intended users, product and exposure rather than assuming consumer-product clearance.

resources.title: Penn State OPEN Design Lab — ANSUR II
resources.use: Find anthropometric background and investigate variation when planning physical fit.
resources.check: US Army sample, not a representative civilian population. Read variable definitions, population and dataset terms; validate fit with intended users.

resources.title: IEC — IEC 62366-1 usability engineering
resources.use: Identify the medical-device usability-engineering standard and its safety-related scope.
resources.check: Public catalog summary only; paid full standard not read or reproduced. Confirm applicable edition/amendments; do not impose medical-device compliance on unrelated products.

resources.title: FDA — Applying Human Factors and Usability Engineering to Medical Devices
resources.use: Study intended users, environments, critical tasks and evaluation of use-related risks in medical-device work.
resources.check: Medical-device guidance. Its validation participant recommendations are context-specific, not a universal product-testing sample size.

resources.title: Ellen MacArthur Foundation — Circular Design Guide
resources.use: Explore useful life, repair, reuse and material recovery when comparing design directions.
resources.check: Methods to investigate; do not claim circularity, recyclability or sustainability without evidence for the product and its actual recovery route.

resources.title: IDEO.org — Design Kit
resources.use: Use human-centered research, concept development and prototyping methods to learn from people.
resources.check: Select methods for the current question. Workshop outputs and positive reactions are not proof of demand, safety or production readiness.

resources.title: FDA — Classify your medical device
resources.use: Official first step for anything that diagnoses, treats or monitors a health problem: is it a device, and which class (I, II, III).
resources.check: Decide whether the intended use makes it a medical device at all. The class sets how heavy the road is. Confirm with a regulatory professional before relying on it.

resources.title: FDA — Product classification database
resources.use: Search similar existing devices to find the likely device class, product code and regulation number.
resources.check: Search by what the product does, not its brand name. Record the product code and class found, and that it is a starting point, not a ruling.

resources.title: FDA — Premarket submissions (510(k), De Novo, PMA)
resources.use: Which submission a device class usually needs before it can be sold.
resources.check: Read after the class is known. Note exemptions. This is professional territory; prepare the material, then get help.

resources.title: FDA — Packaging and food contact substances
resources.use: What materials touching food or drink must meet.
resources.check: Ask the material supplier for its food-contact statement for the exact grade. Keep it with the material record.

resources.title: CPSC — Children’s products
resources.use: Rules for products made for children 12 and under: third-party testing at an accepted lab, a Children’s Product Certificate, tracking labels.
resources.check: Decide first whether it is a children’s product by its intended user. If yes, plan the lab test and certificate before selling. Use with the Regulatory Robot.

resources.title: FAA — Drones (UAS)
resources.use: Official starting point for anything that is, or goes on, a drone.
resources.check: Check registration, operating rules and any product requirements that apply to the drone it goes on.

resources.title: FAA — Aircraft certification
resources.use: Starting point for parts installed on certified aircraft.
resources.check: Parts on certified aircraft need approval; this is a professional road from the start. Record who would install it and on what.

resources.title: FCC — Equipment authorization
resources.use: Plain starting point for selling anything with radio or fast digital electronics in the U.S.: which approval path, labs and FCC ID search.
resources.check: Find the approval procedure for the device type. Look up the FCC ID of any radio module used. Pair with the eCFR part 15 entries.

resources.title: Your Europe — CE marking
resources.use: Official EU starting point: which products need CE marking and the steps to apply it.
resources.check: Only when selling into the EU. Identify which EU rules apply to the product type; keep the technical file and declaration.

resources.title: California Proposition 65 — For businesses
resources.use: Warning-label rules for products sold to California that contain listed chemicals.
resources.check: Ask suppliers whether materials contain listed chemicals. Small businesses under the employee threshold may be exempt; retailers may still ask.

resources.title: SBA — Get business insurance
resources.use: Plain explanation of business insurance types, including product liability, and how to buy it.
resources.check: Use when the inventor declines a company and the liability stays with them, or when a store requires coverage. An agent confirms what a policy covers.

resources.title: CPSC — Recalls and product safety warnings
resources.use: Search recalls on similar products by product type and hazard. What went wrong for others is the cheapest start on the FMEA.
resources.check: Search the product category and the hazard. A clean history does not mean a design is safe; CPSC relies on reports, not pre-market review.

resources.title: SaferProducts.gov — Consumer incident reports
resources.use: Public reports of injuries and hazards with consumer products, often before a recall exists.
resources.check: Search similar products; note hazards that recur. Reports are unverified consumer accounts.

resources.title: USPTO — Patent Public Search
resources.use: The USPTO's own full-text search of U.S. patents and published applications, for a first look at what exists.
resources.check: A search is not a patentability or freedom-to-operate opinion. Record queries, dates and document numbers.

ip_reference.title: IP enclosure ratings — basic guide
first_digit: Dust-protected: limited entry permitted without harmful interference.
Dust-tight: no dust entry in the test.
second_digit: Drips with enclosure tilted up to 15°.
Temporary immersion under specified test conditions.
Continuous immersion under specified conditions; check depth and duration.
notes: Read the digits separately: first solids/dust, then water. The first digit also addresses access to hazardous parts; this is a simplified ingress table.
X means no protection level is specified for that digit; it is not the same as 0.

IPX7 is commonly summarized as a 1 m, 30-minute immersion test. Exact depth/reference points depend on enclosure size and the standard; verify the actual test report. It is not an unlimited underwater-use rating.
IPX7/IPX8 immersion does not automatically establish IPX5/IPX6 jet protection. Where both are needed, verify both ratings, such as IP66/IP67.
Use the rating of the final installed assembly: seals, cable entries, connectors, doors and mounting matter. An enclosure rating alone does not prove the finished product has it.
IP does not establish corrosion, UV, impact, explosion or overall electrical-safety performance. NEMA Types and IP codes are not interchangeable.

government_site_guidance.scope: U.S. government services, with verified partner exceptions
points: For U.S. government registration, start on the agency’s .gov website. U.S. military agencies also use .mil. Do not start from a sponsored search result or an unsolicited renewal link.
SAM registration and renewal are free. An EIN is free when obtained directly from the IRS. State business filing fees can be legitimate; distinguish the government’s fee from an optional service fee.
Read the actual hostname, not the logo or the words in a page title. sam.gov.example.com is part of example.com, not sam.gov. HTTPS protects the connection; it does not prove government identity.

Some real state portals and official partner programs use .us, .org, .edu or commercial domains. Reach them through the verified agency page or its directory and verify the referral. A non-.gov site is not automatically fraudulent or official.

Before entering tax IDs, identity documents, bank details or payment information, verify the agency and exact task. Show the person the official starting URL, final destination and any government versus service fee. Do not rely on a threatening email to verify itself.
For international projects, use that country’s official government directory; .gov and .mil here describe U.S. starting points.

selection_guidance.patent_help: A good match depends on the assigned person’s active registration, relevant technical work, conflicts, communication, written scope and fees. A patent agent’s authority differs from an attorney’s business-law practice. Use USPTO and state licensing records. Named firms are candidates to interview, not a quality ranking.
selection_guidance.prototype_shop: Compare quotes against the same drawing/model revision, material, finish, quantity, tolerance, test and inspection requirements. Check who makes the part, where, lead time, delivered cost, confidentiality and applicable data-sharing restrictions. Keep supplier choice open.
selection_guidance.funding: Match geography, sector, stage, traction and founder criteria before applying. Check fees, confidentiality and sharing terms. A directory or network listing is not a funding promise. Rewards crowdfunding is distinct from equity investment.
selection_guidance.marketing: Start with the customer and evidence of demand. Choose channels, training and tools for that job. Keep advertising claims supportable; verify current channel and legal rules before publication.
